  • Method Details

    • region

      public HudPanel.Builder region(InsideRegion region)
      Where on the game window the panel sits: one of the nine InsideRegion spots, 4px in from the edges it touches. Panels on one spot stack (2px apart) in priority order; CENTER starts just below the crosshair. Required.

    • offset

      public HudPanel.Builder offset(int dx, int dy)
      A pixel nudge after placement (positive x right, positive y down). Only this panel moves; its siblings on the spot stack as if it had not.

      Migrating from .anchor(MKHudAnchor.X, dx, dy): the anchor sat on the window edge, a region sits 4px in. Keep the old pixel position with .region(InsideRegion.X).offset(dx', dy') where each axis that touched an edge gives back the inset: dx' = dx + 4 on a right spot, dx - 4 on a left one; the same for dy on bottom and top spots. A centred axis keeps its offset. The one exception is CENTER: the old anchor centred the panel on the window, while InsideRegion.CENTER on the HUD starts 16px below the centre (clear of the crosshair), so the old CENTER, dx, dy is offset(dx, dy - 16 - panelHeight / 2); for "just below the crosshair", .region(InsideRegion.CENTER) alone says it.

    • priority

      public HudPanel.Builder priority(int priority)
      Stacking order among panels on the same spot (lower is nearer the spot's edge), and render order (lower draws first). Default PanelPosition.DEFAULT_PRIORITY. Ties break by mod id, then by registration order.

    • padding

      public HudPanel.Builder padding(int padding)
      Sets inner padding (space between panel edge and content).

    • autoSize

      public HudPanel.Builder autoSize()
      Sizes the panel to its content. This is the default (a HUD panel is a Panel, which measures its elements); kept so existing builders read the same.

    • size

      public HudPanel.Builder size(int width, int height)
      Sets an explicit outer panel size, padding included.

    • style

      public HudPanel.Builder style(PanelStyle style)
      Sets the panel background style (RAISED, DARK, INSET, NONE). Default NONE.

    • visibleWhen

      public HudPanel.Builder visibleWhen(BooleanSupplier condition)
      The panel shows only while this is true (the panel's own Panel.visibleWhen(BooleanSupplier)). A hidden panel is not measured and takes no room in its spot's stack. To hide while a screen is open (the old hideInScreen()), include it: .visibleWhen(() -> Minecraft.getInstance().gui.screen() == null && ...).

    • custom

      public HudPanel.Builder custom(int childX, int childY, int width, int height, Consumer<RenderContext> renderFn)
      Adds a custom render region. The lambda receives the per-frame RenderContext for its position and graphics handle. The declared width/height are the element's bounds for layout.
      Parameters:
      childX - panel-relative X position
      childY - panel-relative Y position
      width - region width (used for auto-sizing)
      height - region height (used for auto-sizing)
      renderFn - render callback invoked each frame

    • element

      public HudPanel.Builder element(PanelElement element)
      Adds any panel element directly. Escape hatch for consumers that implement PanelElement themselves.

    • build

      public Panel build()
      Builds the HUD panel and registers it; from then on it renders every frame the in-game HUD draws (never with input: the HUD routes none). A HUD panel is an ordinary Panel positioned screenAnchor(region).offset(dx, dy).priority(p) in the HUD's host.
      Returns:
      the panel (for its id, or to toggle its visibility)
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if no region was set, or after MenuKit's declarations froze at client start
